title: Predictive prefetch & telemetry-driven weight proxy spec
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a telemetry-driven, lightweight Weight Proxy that performs predictive prefetching of model parameters (weights) and coordinates with the KV cache priming logic to reduce cold-start latency and improve steady-state tail latency for multi-model, multi-tenant serving. The approach emphasizes safety (no silent corruption), predictable resource budgets, and graceful fallback to mmap-on-demand or safetensors-streaming when predictions are wrong or IO is constrained.

Context and motivation
- Our existing runtime supports on-demand mmap, lazy loading, and safetensors unpacking. These are robust but can produce tail latency outliers when requests reference rarely-used layers or long, branching prompts that cause unexpected layer access patterns.
- We observe two common regimes: (1) warm model, hot KV cache: requests are mostly cache hits but occasional layers miss and trigger IO; (2) cold/warm transitions during rollouts or canary where many requests reference slightly different prefixes.
- A small amount of predictive prefetch (guided by live telemetry) can avoid many of the transient IO spikes and reduce token-level latency without overloading IO.

Goals and constraints
- Goals: reduce 95th/99th token latency by preempting IO; reduce cold-start latency for model variants; integrate with existing KV cache priming to leverage runtime attention patterns.
- Constraints: respect GPU memory budget and system IO budget; must not degrade steady-state throughput; must be safe to abort/revert (no partial corruptions); must be conservative by default (opt-in to aggressive prefetch per model/route).

High-level design
Components:
1) Weight Proxy (lightweight user-space daemon embedded in serving process): receives telemetry, computes prefetch plan, issues fetch requests (local mmap residency, remote blobstore prefetch).
2) Telemetry Collector (in-runtime): emits compact signals per request/route (layer access histogram, token-level KV access counters, latency spikes). Telemetry is aggregated locally with fixed-size sliding windows.
3) Prefetch Planner: attaches to Weight Proxy and turns telemetry into scored candidates for prefetch. Uses a scoring function combining recency, frequency, positional probability (where in transformer stack hits occur), and cost (bytes, IO latency).
4) Priority Coalescer Queue: coalesces overlapping prefetch requests to prevent duplicate IO and enforces an IO budget.
5) Hot-swap Safety Layer: safe activation protocol for weights that ensures kernels don't read incomplete tensors; integrates with safetensors checksum verification.
6) KV cache priming hook: when the planner predicts that upcoming requests will hit specific KV ranges, it signals the KV cache priming module to retain or precompute attention keys for those ranges (best-effort).

Telemetry signals (compact form)
- per-request: route_id, model_id, prefix_length, top-layer-accesses (top N layer indices touched), max-kv-depth, attention-pattern-hash (64-bit), request_latency_ms
- aggregate windows: layer-hit-counts[0..L-1] (uint16 saturation), layer-hot-run-length, failing-io-count, recent-prefetch-success-rate
- runtime counters: current-mmap-residency-bytes, outstanding-fetches, last-safetensors-verify-time
Notes: telemetry intentionally limited to small integers to avoid overhead. No request text leaves the process.

Scoring function (sketch)
score(layer) = alpha*recent_hits(layer) + beta*recency_decay(layer) - gamma*(bytes(layer)/io_bandwidth_budget) - delta*switch_cost(layer)
Where:
- recent_hits: exponentially decayed count in window
- recency_decay: penalty for layers not seen recently
- switch_cost: estimated disruption (if swapping out other weights)
Coefficients tuned per-tenant and per-model. Default is conservative: alpha=1.0 beta=0.6 gamma=0.9 delta=0.3.

Priority Coalescer Queue
- Prefetch requests are de-duplicated by (model_id, shard_range) and consolidated into a single IO operation when possible.
- Queue enforces two budget tokens: IO tokens (bytes/sec) and activation tokens (number of tensors allowed to be promoted into GPU memory per second).
- Policy: short-term burst allowed up to burst_limit, then throttled to steady bandwidth.
- Coalescer can downgrade prefetches to "metadata-only" fetch (load tensor headers and checksum) to verify priority before full data transfer.

Interaction with mmap and safetensors
- Preferred path: if model artifacts are stored as pre-sharded safetensors blobs, the proxy requests remote fetching of the needed shards into an intermediate cache (local SSD or tmpfs) followed by async mmap into the serving process.
- Fallback: if intermediate cache or remote fetch is slow, fall back to on-demand mmap streaming (existing lazy loader).
- For safetensors we verify integrity of each shard via checksums before mapping. If checksum fails, proxy triggers artifact-repair workflow (log + notify) and falls back to safe on-demand streaming.

Hot-swap safety and activation protocol
- Activation handshake (atomic switch):
  1) Proxy fetches full shard into local staging area and computes checksum.
  2) Proxy requests runtime to pin the target tensor memory region while copy completes. Kernel readers remain pinned on old pointer until activation commit.
  3) Commit step is a single atomic pointer swap + update of residency table. We use generation counters to ensure in-flight kernels ignore new generation until they re-sample the residency map.
  4) If activation fails, proxy rolls back by unmapping staging area and leaving previous residency untouched.
- Readers must observe generation counters. This requires minimal runtime cooperation: before kernel read, check generation == current; if mismatch, retry read after small backoff. This avoids tearing.

KV cache priming integration
- The planner emits "KV prime buckets" (layer, kv-offset-range, probability). The KV priming subsystem uses these hints to prefetch or pin KV ranges in GPU memory or host-pinned memory.
- Priming is best-effort and bounded by an independent KV budget to avoid starving weight prefetch. If KV priming conflicts with weight activation, weights get priority for the first 200ms of a canary rollout window.

Budgeting and failure modes
- Budget controls exist at process-level and tenant-level: max_prefetch_bytes, max_active_tensors, io_bandwidth_limit, safetensors_verify_workers.
- Failure modes: prediction misses (no actual accesses) —> harmless wasted IO, tracked by prefetch_hit_rate metric.
- IO contention: if io queue backlog grows beyond threshold, the proxy signals throttling and can downgrade prefetches to header-only.
- Safety: checksums + activation handshake ensure we never map corrupted tensors into GPU memory.

Experimentation and rollout plan
- Phase 0 (lab): run offline replay from historical telemetry to tune scoring coefficients. Measure simulated latency improvements and wasted bytes.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable proxy in read-only mode (issue prefetch requests but do not activate hot-swap) on 5% of traffic for selected models. Measure prefetch hit rate and IO impact.
- Phase 2 (soft-activation): allow hot-swap activation for canary models with strict budgets. Monitor error rates and kernel retries.
- Phase 3 (gradual rollout): increase to 25% then 50% with tenant opt-in.

Metrics and instrumentation
- Prefetch_hit_rate (per model, per route)
- Prefetch_bytes_wasted
- Avg and p95 token latency delta pre/post prefetch
- Activation_failures and rollback_count
- IO_queue_length and verify_worker_utilization
- KV_prime_success_rate

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How aggressive should scoring be for small shards vs big tensors? We avoid large contiguous tensors unless likely to be used.
- Generation counters: minimal overhead vs kernel complexity. Need SRE & kernel authors to validate that retries don't add harmful jitter.
- Multi-tenant fairness: should we globalize budgets or per-tenant? Proposal: per-process budgets with tenant-weighted share enforced by proxy.
- Telemetry privacy: keep signals compact and per-process; do not export request text.

Implementation notes / TODOs
- [ ] Prototype Prefetch Planner in Python to validate scoring on replay traces (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Implement lightweight Weight Proxy binary (Rust recommended) with simple HTTP+unix-socket control plane (owner: Alejandro).
- [ ] Add generation-counter support to runtime immune-kernel path (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Add safetensors shard header-only fetch API to artifact store (owner: Storage team ticketed).
- [ ] Create dashboards for prefetch_hit_rate, wasted_bytes, activation_rollbacks (owner: Ben).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally conservative: primary goal is to reduce transient IO spikes without risking model correctness. Comments sought on scoring heuristics and budget defaults.
- If we agree on activation handshake semantics, we can reuse much of the existing lazy-loader code and add the proxy as an optional layer in front of artifact access.

References
- internal: JIRA RUNTIME-342 (lazy loader), RUNTIME-410 (KV cache priming), GHD-2112 (artifact safetensors layout)
- external: safetensors spec, mmap best practices, prior art from other inference runtimes

End of doc.
